newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telebras rises in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telebras rises in New York.

text.p: Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose Tuesday to stand out among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Telebras was up 4-1/4 to 156 in moderate trade that put it among the most active ADRs in New York. The ADRs had closed Friday at 154-3/8 before falling Monday.
"We're seeing a little bit of a rebound here," a trader said, noting that Brazil's local market also was up after recent dips.
Traders said Telebras's decline on Monday had come as institutional investors readjusted their portfolios at the end of the second quarter.

In addition, Credit Suisse First Boston and HSBC James Capel cut their ratings Monday for the ADRs, which have risen from a 12-month low of 69. The downgrades came in part because the company announced its subsidiaries would sell new shares worth almost two billion reais.
In a report Tuesday, Smith Barney analyst Peter Treadway said the Telebras move had been misunderstood by the market and was a "financial plus but possibly a public relations black eye."
He kept his rating of outperform for Telebras.
In other active ADRs, offshore oil contractor Stolt Comex Seaway SA was up 3-5/8, or more than 14 percent, to a 12-month high of 29. The ADRs were among percentage gain leaders on the Nasdaq.

The rise came after the company, a subsidiary of Stolt-Nielsen SA, reported a second-quarter profit of $0.62 a share against a loss of $1.28 in the same period a year before. Stolt-Nielsen was up 7/8 to 19-3/4.

Canadian drug company BioChem Pharma Inc was up 3/8 to 22-5/8 in heavy trade. British drug ADRs rose, with Glaxo Wellcome Plc up 1-10/16 to a 12-month high of 43-7/16 and SmithKline Beecham Plc up 3-3/8 to 95, also a year's high.
Advancers led decliners 265 to 210 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.21 percent by late morning and volume was 28.6 million shares.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
